plans.angle: REVENUE-FIRST: one SKU (prepaid API/MCP credit packs for AI-agent developers), the web app demoted to a free marketing surface, everything that does not sit on the sign-in -> pay -> mint-key -> curl path is cut or deferred.
plans.thesis: OpenCITE's only sellable thing today is credits spendable on /api/search, /api/citations and /api/ids via an API key - and that path is missing exactly four cheap pieces (a live database, a key-mint UI, a pack->machine plan assignment, and a page that tells a developer the thing exists), plus three non-code prerequisites (Vercel Pro so payments are policy-legal, an OpenAlex project key so the flagship source does not go dark after ~50 queries/day, and a published ToS/privacy/refund surface so Stripe disputes are not automatic losses). Every other revenue lever is either fake (web subscriptions sell entitlements the browser already gives away free; Student is unpurchasable) or structurally expensive (routing web search through the meter costs ~16h and burns the OpenAlex budget for no reason-to-buy). So the bet is: delete the subscription/Student rail from the UI instead of building the gating it would need, reprice packs to cost-plus ($5/1k instead of $0.67-1.00/1k, still the cheapest metered scholarly search API), thread `limit` through to the adapters and drop the six dead-but-200 sources so a paid query is actually worth $0.005, then spend the last ten days of the month on distribution (npm-published MCP, served OpenAPI/docs, README rewritten around heritage/Islamicate breadth + citation formats + coverage-honest billing, a Show HN and 20 direct DMs). With zero traffic, the first dollar is a distribution event, not an engineering one - the engineering just has to stop the customer from bouncing off a 401, a 403, an empty result set, or a missing legal page. Target: first external $10 pack by day 21-30; ~54 founder-hours with Claude Code.
plans.mvp_definition: A developer who has never spoken to Shahbaz can, on citation.today: (1) sign in with Google (Supabase restored, sessions live); (2) open a Developers panel, buy a $10 pack (2,000 credits) through Stripe with a published ToS/privacy/refund page and consent checkbox; (3) land back on the Developers panel, see the credits, mint an API key (plaintext shown once); (4) run the curl snippet from that panel or `npx opencite-mcp` with the key and receive an interleaved, DOI-deduped, coverage-honest response of up to `limit` results from ~18 live serverSafe sources (OpenAlex on a project key; BASE/Met/PANGAEA/Thaqalayn/OpenContext/LA Referencia removed from the billable set); (5) see the balance decrement, with the buyer on plan=machine (all tier, 300/min). The web search app stays free, unmetered and unchanged; the Plans panel no longer shows Free/Student/Pro cards; main == prod at a known SHA; an uptime probe exercises a DB-touching route; Vercel is on Pro. No credit_events journal, no remote MCP, no account deletion, no engine - those are post-first-dollar.

plans.angle: RISK/STABILITY-FIRST — recover the data, make prod reproducible, make the ledger auditable, then sell exactly one SKU (developer credit packs) through one honest path.
plans.thesis: OpenCITE cannot take a dollar today without creating an incident: the only copy of every user/key/credit row sits in a paused Free-plan Supabase project whose one-click restore window closes in roughly 11-18 days; production is an unreproducible mid-sprint snapshot that any push to main would silently overwrite; the credit ledger is a single mutable number with no journal, a webhook that can swallow paid grants, and copy that promises entitlements the code never delivers. The bet is to spend the first ~10 days on zero new features — restore + off-site dump, commit-what-prod-runs, monitoring, Vercel Pro, and the v0.45/v0.46 money-path closure — and only then open a single revenue mechanism: developer/agent credit packs (plan=machine) sold with a Developers panel that mints API keys, priced cost-plus above OpenAlex's metered rate, behind published ToS/privacy/refund pages. steps.what: src/constants/pricing.js + Panels.jsx: hide Student and Pro cards (keep code behind a `SUBSCRIPTIONS_ENABLED=false` flag), rewrite the Plans panel as two truths — 'Web app: free, all sources, no limits' and 'API & MCP credits for your AI' — derive SOURCE_COUNT from the adapter registry, delete the IAP/App Store rail strings. api/stripe/webhook.js pack branch: gate on `payment_status === 'paid'` (and handle checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded), set `plan:'machine'` when current plan is free. api/_shared: seed free users with 20 credits via a lazy grant in resolveApiKey/credits handler when credits_period != current month (FREE_MONTHLY_GRANT SSOT). steps.name: Make the metered answer worth paying for
steps.what: Thread `opts.pageSize = Math.min(limit, adapterMax)` from api/search.js through runSearch into every adapter (keep browser 3/5 defaults); order interleave lanes by a static precision rank (OpenAlex, Crossref, DOAJ, Europe-PMC-style sources first, heritage after) instead of registry order; require ≥ceil(n/2) meaningful terms in hasContentMatch for Crossref; return 400/503 when `adapters.length === 0` before preAuthorize and map coverage total===0 → 'limited'; include `cite` in cacheKey (or cache pre-render records and render per request); add `version:'2'` to API_CONTRACT echoed as X-OpenCITE-API-Version and folded into the cache key.
steps.why: A free-tier query today returns ≤12 candidates regardless of limit, with off-topic Crossref hits at ranks 3/6/9 — an agent developer will churn on the first call. These four changes are what make 'citation-ready sources across papers + archives' true.

steps.name: Adapter honesty: quarantine the dead, fix Gallica, unbreak the proxy
steps.what: Flip serverSafe:false / quarantine (v0.44 T5 pattern) BASE, THAQALAYN, LA_REFERENCIA, PANGAEA, OPENCONTEXT; fix MET by dropping artistOrCulture=true (0.5h); rewrite api/search/gallica.js to the xmlUtils regex SRU helpers (inline under api/_shared) so the heritage flagship works; make every shim adapter `throw` on `data.error` (mirror europeana.js:49); add data.rijksmuseum.nl, api.core.ac.uk, ndl.iitkgp.ac.in to ALLOWED_DOMAINS and remove the five quarantined hosts; add AbortSignal.timeout(10s) to api/proxy.js; treat upstream error bodies as adapter failures in base.js-style parsers.
steps.why: Six sources return 200-with-nothing and inflate the coverage band, so paying customers are charged 'full' for a library that is >30% unreachable, while the one heritage source developers will demo (Gallica) has never worked in prod.

steps.name: Polite-pool identity and honest User-Agent
steps.what: Shared server fetch wrapper sets `User-Agent: OpenCITE/<APP_VERSION> (https://citation.today; mailto:<role address>)`; hard-code a fallback mailto when OPENCITE_MAILTO is unset; ncbi.js appends tool/email/api_key; drop the Chrome UA spoof in proxy.js server branch; ignore caller-supplied `mailto` on the metered API (always project identity).
steps.why: Crossref drops to 1 req/s without mailto (live-verified) and NCBI's 3 req/s shared budget guarantees 429s at machine-plan rates; also removes the ToS-violation surface with NCBI/Open Library.

steps.name: Metering-edge hardening before onboarding paying callers
steps.what: Run a per-IP KV limiter before any DB touch on /api/search, /api/citations, /api/ids (apply to the 401 path); reject malformed keys by regex before hashing; move/debounce last_used_at (≥60 s); drop `?key=` query support (header only); cap `;` terms at 5 and q length at 512 in apiContract.js; key checkRateLimit on userId; cap /api/proxy streamed bytes at 2 MB with an Edge-style Sec-Fetch-Site soft guard; silently intersect unknown `sources=` ids instead of 400.
steps.why: An attacker with no credential can drive unbounded Postgres traffic through pgBouncer, a single credit can fan out thousands of upstream calls, and bearer keys would land in request logs — all cheap to fix now, expensive after the first customer.

steps.name: Webhook correctness for real money

risks: Supabase one-click restore window (~2026-09-15..22) closes before step 1 runs → falls back to backup-download + new project + env rewrite, adding ~4 h and a new project ref.

Demand risk is unvalidated: 0 stars, 0 traffic, and free MIT MCPs (paper-search-mcp 2.6k stars) cover the paper half; the heritage/Islamicate edge may be too niche to convert 10 DMs into one $10 pack in 30 days.

OpenAlex economics: even with a free key the $1/day allowance caps ~1,000 search calls; one enthusiastic agent user can exhaust it and every later customer sees a 'partial' band that day until prepaid credits are added.
Vercel may act on the existing Hobby fair-use violation (Ko-fi + checkout in the live bundle) before the Pro upgrade lands.

The single `git add -A` commit is blocked by the pre-commit hook until the ledger fragments are fixed; if --check cannot be made green in 3 h the fallback is a documented `--no-verify` commit of the exact tree prod runs, which conflicts with the PowerShell tool's no-skip-hooks rule and must be Shahbaz's call.
Stripe API-version shape on the webhook endpoint is unverifiable from the repo; if it is basil, first-invoice handling is wrong the day subscriptions are re-enabled (mitigated in step 12).

Upstream ToS exposure remains for Internet Archive ('scholarship and research only') and BnF attribution in an origin-blind paid contract; a Sources/attribution page or serverSafe flip may be required if challenged.

Claude/ChatGPT directory requirements (upstream disclosure, no in-app checkout links) conflict with the 'origin-blind' positioning and the 402→Plans link; the 90-day directory step may require abandoning origin-blindness publicly.
Solo bandwidth: the 30-day plan is ~59 h of agent-assisted work plus dashboard tasks; any Supabase or Stripe incident consumes the buffer.
Legal pages written without counsel carry residual risk on refunds and consumer law in the EU/UK; mitigated by pack-only sales and a 14-day unused-credit withdrawal clause.

Persona mismatch: if early users are pure CS/bio developers rather than humanities researchers, the heritage differentiation will not drive conversion and the plan must pivot to citation-graph/ID-resolution as the lead feature.

scores.angle: REVENUE-FIRST: one SKU (prepaid API/MCP credit packs), web app demoted to free marketing surface, everything off the sign-in→pay→mint→curl path cut or deferred
scores.strengths: (a) Time-to-first-dollar 7/10: the most direct line to a working curl — Supabase restore day 1, deploy freeze + Pro same day, key UI by day 8, real-card smoke day 13, distribution days 14-30; the plan is explicit that with zero traffic 'the first dollar is a distribution event' and budgets 6h of hand-selling plus Show HN/DMs. (b) P0s 8/10: DB restore + off-site dump + keepalive + migrate.mjs password-redaction all in step 1; deploy footgun frozen in step 2 (Git prod deploys disabled, Dependabot PRs closed); key path (Developers panel on existing /api/keys) at step 6; pack→plan=machine + payment_status gate at step 5. (c) Effort 6/10: per-step estimates are individually plausible and the 30-day set (~54h) is itemized; sensible shortcuts (rename free allowance to '10 free credits' instead of building the grant sweep; flip serverSafe:false instead of fixing six dead adapters; minimal fragment edits to pass the pre-commit hook). (d) Market 6/10: reprices to $5/1k cost-plus, sells the three real differentiators, offers 100 trial credits, removes the fake subscription rail so the offer is true. (e) Cuts 9/10: the longest and sharpest cut list of the three — no web gating, no Student, no dead-adapter fixes, no v0.45 journal before ten customers, no directory listings before remote MCP exists, no wiki rewrite, no a11y/perf, Ko-fi removed, IAP rail deleted, `;`/`?key=` removed rather than documented. Correctly identifies that hiding the subscription cards closes six findings by deletion instead of 16h of gating.
scores.weaknesses: Commit of the 152-file dirty tree does not happen until step 10 (day 13), so ~12 days of money-path edits accrue on top of an already-unreproducible prod snapshot; a mistake or interruption before then leaves main even further from prod (mitigated only by the Git-deploy freeze in step 2). No refund/dispute clawback until the 90-day step 15 — a refunded $200 pack keeps 60k credits, covered only by a 'manual procedure documented in refunds.html'; Plan 2 shows this is a 2h item and should be in-window. Monitoring lands at step 11, after all the money-path code, though step 1's health handler + cron partially covers it. Step 8 is under-estimated: threading pageSize through ~28 adapter files + six serverSafe flips + five shim `throw`s + interleave lane reorder + Crossref match tightening + cache-key + AbortSignal polyfill is closer to 10-12h than 7h, so the true 30-day total is ~65-75h, not 54h. Free-tier developers get only the seeded 10 credits (advertised '20/month' finding closed by copy change, which is fine, but nothing itemizes adding an upgrade link to the bare `Insufficient credits.` 402 body, so the out-of-credits moment has no conversion hook). Legal step ships without counsel and with no Stripe Tax/billing-address capture beyond the address field — acceptable at $10 but noted. Step 12 targets Smithery/Glama/PulseMCP listing before any usage data; fine but it is the only distribution that does not require Shahbaz's time.

scores.angle: RISK/STABILITY-FIRST: recover data, make prod reproducible, make the ledger auditable, then sell one SKU (developer credit packs) through one honest path

(c) Effort honesty 7/10: the only plan that states its real 30-day number (~78h, 'no slack') and names which steps to cut down if it slips (legal step 12 to two pages + deletion; quarantine before Gallica fix). Names the unexplained 2026-07-05 'iss missing' OAuth failure as a second auth defect to check on first live sign-in — a genuinely useful catch none of the others has. (d) Market 6/10: same repriced pack SKU, same three differentiators, self-purchase + refund test before a stranger pays. (a) 5/10 and (e) 5/10 see weaknesses.

Monetization surface is opened only at step 9-11, so a solo founder spends ~3 weeks with zero external signal on whether anyone wants the SKU.
